concepts.def: Timber from broadleaved deciduous trees such as oak and beech, generally denser and slower-growing than softwoods.
Timber from coniferous trees such as pine and spruce, faster-growing and widely used for construction and furniture frames.
Engineered timber product such as MDF, plywood or chipboard, providing dimensional stability and large sheet sizes.
Manufactured board of thin veneers glued with grain at right angles, giving strength in both directions.
Controlled drying of timber to reduce moisture content, minimising warping and improving workability.
Medium-density fibreboard made from compressed wood fibres and resin, valued for smooth surfaces and ease of machining.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Materials & Applications — a core area of A-Level Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Materials & Applications brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Materials & Applications.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
